suggestion: Run the capture jobs from GitHub Actions instead of a workstation
options: (a) stay manual, (b) scheduled runner with hash retention, (c) third-party archive
recommendation: (b): the repo already proves runners can reach nfl.com; captures land as versioned files with hashes
acceptance_test: Two weekly captures arrive with valid hashes
what_would_change_our_mind: If the NFL refuses automated retrieval in writing, fall back to (a) with a once-daily manual capture and keep aggregates only.

suggestion: Buy the missing side of the availability graph: official inactives
options: (a) keep using playing time, (b) read the official inactives article weekly, (c) infer inactives from snap counts
recommendation: (b): it is official, dated, and covers every game; (c) is inference and is rejected
cost: MEDIUM — a weekly read plus a join
acceptance_test: 32/32 clubs with an official inactive list per week
what_would_change_our_mind: If the inactives article is not reliably published before kickoff, keep (a) and publish the join rate.

suggestion: Stop trying to beat the closing line with public game-level data
options: (a) keep tuning the same model, (b) move to the availability and matchup questions, (c) keep the model as a benchmark generator
recommendation: (c) plus (b): the model's job becomes producing a residual series, not a bet signal
acceptance_test: The residual series is published weekly and the bets stay in paper
what_would_change_our_mind: If a point-in-time availability feature lifts Brier skill above zero on the holdout, revisit.

suggestion: Adopt the operator-attributed price store as the only market source
options: (a) keep aggregator lines, (b) two named operators with read stamps, (c) a paid feed
recommendation: (b) now, (c) only if a legal feed is found
acceptance_test: Two operators captured at kickoff for four consecutive weeks
what_would_change_our_mind: If one operator stops serving the page or changes its terms, drop to one book and stop publishing consensus claims.

suggestion: Publish the designation study weekly as its own product
recommendation: (b): the play rate is a decision input for every injury story and nobody publishes intervals
what_would_change_our_mind: If the rate is flat at 25% all season, publish (b) as a single stable number instead.

suggestion: Replace the 'depth chart' idea with a usage-rank table
options: (a) parse 32 club depth pages, (b) usage ranks from playing time, (c) both
recommendation: (b): it is measurable, uniform, and free of jersey-order errors; (a) is where the two parsing failures came from
acceptance_test: Reviewer acceptance of usage rank as the depth definition
what_would_change_our_mind: If a club publishes an official structured depth feed, add it as a cross-check and publish disagreements.

suggestion: Make the demotion gate a two-sided test on the skill interval
what_would_change_our_mind: If the gate demotes every strategy in the first month, widen it once and publish the change as a new registration.

suggestion: Retire the 136-game log as a corpus and keep it as an audit artefact
options: (a) patch the 19 rows, (b) retire it, (c) keep both
recommendation: (a) then (b): patch first so the audit is complete, then point the corpus at the pinned dataset only
what_would_change_our_mind: If the official week pages are unavailable for the missing rows, retire immediately with the gap published.

suggestion: Publish the residual every week, not the pick
options: (a) publish picks, (b) publish the residual series, (c) publish both
recommendation: (b): a residual series accumulates evidence whether or not anyone bets; picks invite result-chasing
what_would_change_our_mind: If residuals show a persistent sign, write a new registration for a strategy and test it prospectively.

suggestion: Use one shared data contract for hashes across desks
recommendation: (b): the repo already has six incompatible capture manifests
what_would_change_our_mind: If a desk's owner objects to the schema, keep local formats and publish a one-way mapping.

suggestion: Publish the model card with the failure result on the landing page
options: (a) bury it, (b) headline it, (c) footnote it
recommendation: (b): the most useful output of this session is that the model loses to the line; a reader who misses that is misled
acceptance_test: Reviewer confirms the failure is on the landing page
what_would_change_our_mind: If a later model clears the gate, the headline changes and the failure moves to the model card.

suggestion: Gate combos on measured dependence rather than an opinion
options: (a) block forever, (b) block until r is published with n, (c) allow small combos
recommendation: (b): the dependence is measured (r=0.513 for QB/top-WR), so the block can be lifted with evidence
acceptance_test: A published joint-vs-marginal gap under 1 pp
what_would_change_our_mind: If the joint model cannot be fitted with adequate n, keep (a).
